summary.en: The Venezuelan army has bombed an ELN guerrilla camp in Apure, killing at least 19 rebels, and a drone strike hit an ELN drug depot nearby, causing at least 20 deaths. President Trump boasted about a one-day operation to capture Maduro and warned of possible U.S. action against Cuba while claiming Venezuelan oil revenues far exceed Iran war costs. Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela and called for elections in her first address since returning. Chevron is expanding operations in Venezuela and Exxon is urging caution. The UCDP counted 2 battle-related deaths in 2007.
summary.nb: Den venezuelanske hæren har bombet en ELN-guerrillaleir i Apure, og drept minst 19 opprørere, og et droneangrep traff et ELN-drogdepot i nærheten, som forårsaket minst 20 dødsfall. President Trump skrytte av en ett-dags operasjon for å fange Maduro og advarte om mulig amerikansk handling mot Cuba mens han hevdet at inntektene fra venezuelansk olje langt overgår kostnadene ved krigen i Iran. Opposisjonslederen María Corina Machado kom tilbake til Venezuela og oppfordret til valg i sin første tale siden hun kom tilbake. Chevron utvider virksomheten i Venezuela og Exxon oppfordrer til forsiktighet. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i kamp i 2007.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
